(ii) If we divide the numbers 4, 3, 2, 1 and 0 by 4 and take square root of quotients, we get the values of $\cos 0^\circ$, $\cos 30^\circ$, $\cos 45^\circ$, $\cos 60^\circ$ and $\cos 90^\circ$ respectively.

(iii) If we divide the numbers 0, 1, 3 and 9 by 3 and take square root of the quotients, we get the values of $\tan 0^\circ$, $\tan 30^\circ$, $\tan 45^\circ$ and $\tan 60^\circ$ respectively. (It is noted that $\tan 90^\circ$ is undefined).

(iv) If we divide the numbers 9, 3, 1 and 0 by 3 and take square root of the quotients, we get the values of $\cot 30^\circ$, $\cot 45^\circ$, $\cot 60^\circ$ and $\cot 90^\circ$ respectively. (It is noted that $\cot 0^\circ$ is undefined).

Solution:
1) Given expression = $\dfrac{1 - \sin^2 45^\circ}{1 + \sin^2 45^\circ} + \tan^2 45^\circ$
$= \dfrac{1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2}{1 + \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2} + (1)^2$ $[\because \sin 45^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\tan 45^\circ = 1]$
$= \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{2}} + 1 = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{3}{2}} + 1 = \dfrac{1}{3} + 1 = \dfrac{4}{3}$

2) Given expression = $\cot 90^\circ \cdot \tan 0^\circ \cdot \sec 30^\circ \cdot \text{cosec } 60^\circ$
$= 0 \cdot 0 \cdot \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} = 0$
$[\because \cot 90^\circ = 0, \tan 0^\circ = 0, \sec 30^\circ = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}, \text{cosec } 60^\circ = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}]$

3) Given expression = $\sin 60^\circ \cdot \cos 30^\circ + \cos 60^\circ \cdot \sin 30^\circ$
